election_dates.generalSnippet: 20A-1-201: "(1) A regular general election shall be held throughout the state on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each even-numbered year. (2) At the regular general election, the voters shall: (a) choose persons to serve the terms established by law for the following offices: ... (ii) United States Senators; (iii) Representatives to the United States Congress..."

state_background_check.value: No — Utah's constitution bars convicted felons from holding office in the state until their right is restored (after 10 years, full sentence completion, and restitution), but doesn't operate as a candidate disclosure form the way some other states' do, and the U.S. Constitution's own qualifications for Congress (age, citizenship, residency) can't be added to by any state, so this doesn't reach U.S. House or Senate candidates
state_background_check.snippet: Utah Const. Art. IV, § 6: "Any mentally incompetent person, any person convicted of a felony, or any person convicted of treason or a crime against the elective franchise, may not be permitted to vote at any election or be eligible to hold office in this State until the right to vote or hold elective office is restored as provided by statute." Congressional qualifications are set exclusively by the U.S. Constitution, confirmed per https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R41946.html: "the Framers intended the Constitution to be the exclusive source of qualifications for Members of Congress, and that the Framers thereby 'divested' States of any power to add qualifications."

platform.value: Supports securing the border, ending catch-and-release, and modernizing legal immigration to be orderly and aligned with economic needs.
platform.snippet:
Border security is national security. The federal government has a clear duty to enforce our laws, secure our borders, and stop the flow of fentanyl, human trafficking, and criminal activity that has devastated communities from Utah to the southern border. At the same time, our legal immigration system is broken, outdated, inefficient, and failing both American workers and those trying to come here the right way.

I support securing the border, ending catch and release, and giving the men and women of law enforcement the tools and backing they need to do their jobs. We also need to modernize legal immigration so it's orderly, lawful, and aligned with the needs of our economy, all while upholding the rule of law that makes this country worth coming to in the first place.

platform.value: Favors reducing federal regulation and spending, pushing power back to states and families, to cut red tape on small businesses.
platform.snippet:
Utah has one of the strongest economies in the nation. Our state leads on job creation, entrepreneurship, and economic freedom because Utahns are hardworking, innovative, and trusted to make their own decisions. The best thing the federal government can do for our economy is get out of the way. For too long, Washington has grown bigger while American paychecks have grown smaller. Burdensome regulations, runaway spending, and a tax code that punishes work and investment have made it harder for families to get ahead and for small businesses to compete. I believe the answer isn't more federal programs or another agency in D.C., it's pushing power, dollars, and decisions back to the states, communities, and families who actually live with the consequences.

I'm committed to cutting red tape that strangles small businesses, reining in regulatory agencies that have stretched far beyond their intended purpose, and empowering Utah.

platform.value: As a former family practice physician, supports price transparency, expanded health savings accounts, ending prior-authorization delays, and letting drug rebates go directly to patients rather than middlemen.
platform.snippet:
After more than 25 years as a family practice physician, I've seen our healthcare system from the inside, and I know it's broken. Costs are too high, care is too tangled in red tape, and too many hardworking families are paying more for insurance they can barely afford to use. Making healthcare affordable again is one of my top priorities in Congress.

Since Obamacare passed, deductibles and out-of-pocket costs have skyrocketed, leaving millions of Americans with coverage on paper they can't actually use. I'm leading legislation to put patients back in charge through price transparency and expanded health savings accounts, and to stop the insurance-driven prior authorization requests and mandated step therapies that delay critical care.

On prescription drugs, I support the Trump Administration's efforts to negotiate lower prices, and I've backed legislation to ensure drug rebates go directly to patients rather than getting absorbed by PBMs.

platform.value: Supports caps on discretionary spending and reducing waste, framing the national debt as a burden passed to future generations.
platform.snippet:
Washington has a spending problem and every Utah family knows it. Households across our state balance budgets, plan for the future, and live within their means. Meanwhile, Congress racks up record deficits and passes the bill to our children and grandchildren. That is irresponsible and a moral failure.

I'm committed to restoring regular order. I support meaningful caps on discretionary spending, rooting out waste and duplication across federal agencies, and confronting the long-term drivers of our debt honestly instead of kicking the can down the road.

platform.value: Supports an 'all-of-the-above' energy approach (oil, gas, nuclear, geothermal), state-led resource management, and cutting federal permitting red tape.
platform.snippet: As your Congressman, I understand that affordable and reliable energy is essential to the health, security, and economic well-being of our communities. I support an all-of-the-above energy approach that embraces American oil, natural gas, nuclear, geothermal, and all other energy production. I also recognize that energy independence is critical to keeping costs low for families and businesses. Too often, excessive federal red tape and bureaucratic delays stifle innovation, restrict access to our resources, and undermine the states that are responsibly leading the way in domestic energy production.

bio_summary.value: Jonny Larsen is a Marine combat veteran who grew up in a Salt Lake City trailer park before his mother abandoned him to a group home at thirteen. His grandmother took him in, and her union pension and Social Security shaped his belief in the programs that keep working families afloat. With the help of a tight knit community that stepped in to raise him, he enlisted in the Marines at seventeen. After the Marines, he built a career as a Senior Systems and Network Administrator before using his GI Bill to study applied math and physics at the University of Utah. He ran out of funding before finishing, a reminder that education should be accessible to everyone willing to put in the work. Today he lives in Salt Lake City with his Great Dane Duke and three cats he rescued as kittens.
